newsitem.title: USA: IRIDIUM postpones satellite launch for 2nd time.
newsitem.headline: IRIDIUM postpones satellite launch for 2nd time.

text.p: IRIDIUM LLC on Monday said the launch of its first three satellites was postponed until January 19 at the earliest, as the program encountered technical problems that forced a delay for a second time.

The consortium said a problem was discovered with the thermal protection on the McDonnell Douglas Delta II rocket that was to carry the satellites into orbit. The launch team is working to correct the problem and to establish a recovery schedule for a new launch date, IRIDIUM said.
Motorola Inc has about a 25 percent stake in IRIDIUM, an international consortium that is working to provide a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
The launch was initially scheduled for January 8, but unrelated technical problems forced the consortium to reschedule it for the first time.
The consortium includes a total of 17 companies, including Motorola, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd of Taiwan and Raytheon Co.
